featured_videos.title: Why Everyone's Leaving Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.commentary: Shawn Baker titled this one like a warning, but the 1,400-comment pile-on told a completely different story. The video asks whether people are actually bailing on carnivore, and the answers coming back are things like "83 years old, six years carnivore, no plans to change" and "cured my AFIB, psoriasis, and diverticulitis at 74 and I'm in for the duration." One commenter lost 70 lbs in six months, watched their arthritis disappear, and said flatly that carnivore changed their life. The real story here isn't who's leaving. It's how many people feel like they'd never go back.

featured_videos.title: It Took Me 3 Years on Carnivore to Realize What I'll Tell You in 10 Minutes
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: 3 Years of Carnivore Lessons in 10 Minutes
featured_videos.commentary: This one resonated with a lot of people, and it's easy to see why. The comment section is full of real transformations: a veteran on a strict lion diet losing 100 lbs with autoimmune improvements, a 61-year-old swimming 80 laps a day after dropping 50 lbs, someone logging 200+ lbs lost on OMAD carnivore. The through-line in the comments is carnivore combined with fasting, which tracks with what the research shows about insulin sensitivity improvements when you remove carbohydrates and compress your eating window. If you're early in the process and frustrated with slow results, this video is worth your 10 minutes.

featured_videos.title: I Eat The SAME 5 Ground Beef Meals Every Week (CHEAP Carnivore Meal Plan)
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: 5 Cheap Carnivore Ground Beef Meals, Every Week
featured_videos.commentary: Steak and Butter Gal went full practical this week with a cheap carnivore meal plan built around five ground beef recipes she rotates every single week, and the comments are already riffing on it. Someone shared a skillet meatloaf recipe with pork rinds, bacon, and cheddar cooked in cast iron that sounds genuinely worth trying. Another person is three months in, down 55 lbs, with no acid reflux, no snoring, and no chest pain, eating exactly this kind of budget-friendly approach. This is the video you send someone when they say carnivore is too expensive.

featured_videos.title: SUBSTITUA O PÃO! Só 3 INGREDIENTES, ZERO CARBOIDRATOS, Muita Proteína e Sem Farinha - Delicioso!
featured_videos.creator: Nutricionista Patricia Leite
featured_videos.commentary: This Brazilian recipe channel has found something genuinely useful: a zero-carb bread substitute built on egg whites and parmesan, with no flour and no additives. The comment engagement is high relative to views, which usually means the recipe actually works for people. Egg whites are a nearly perfect protein source, and parmesan adds fat, salt, and flavor without the carbohydrate load. If the biggest barrier keeping you from strict carnivore or zero-carb eating is missing bread's texture, this is worth trying. It's not a magic solution, but it shows how a little creativity in the kitchen makes the long-term approach sustainable.

featured_videos.title: Chris Packham Exposed For Being A Hypocrite
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: When Carnivore Animals Are Forced to Eat Plants
featured_videos.commentary: Dogs are obligate protein-dependent predators. Their gut, their teeth, their entire biology is built to process meat. Kent Carnivore breaks down what happens when a BBC wildlife presenter forces his dogs onto a vegan diet, and the data isn't subtle. One commenter reports zero vet visits in eight years feeding their dog fat and steak. That's a result. The parallel to the carnivore community is direct: when you eat against your evolutionary biology, you pay for it. Packham's dogs are the experiment. The community already knows how the results turn out.

featured_videos.title: After 5,000 Carnivore Patients, I Noticed This Pattern
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Elizabeth Bright
featured_videos.editorial_title: What 5,000 Carnivore Patients Taught One Doctor
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Elizabeth Bright has seen enough carnivore patients to notice patterns most people miss, and this video zeroes in on electrolytes. The consistent issue she flagged, muscle cramps, leg cramps, and disrupted sleep, comes up again and again in her patient pool. The comments add texture: a 70-year-old reporting 35 years of poor sleep now resolved with consistent sea salt intake, and several people connecting it to the sodium-potassium pump and how dramatically sodium requirements shift when you cut carbohydrates. This is one of the most under-discussed parts of the carnivore transition. If you're sleeping badly or cramping, this is where to start.
